findings.excerpt:
· intro ht
    rw [he]
    apply le_of_not_gt
    intro h
    exact (not_le_of_gt ht) (hh.2.1.mpr h.le)
findings.problem: All four side-goal bullets repeat `rw [he]` just to turn `S.Q t ω i` into `logLoewnerCoordinates (G ω) (z i) t`, the form used in the threshold facts `hh`. The two `hbefore`/`hend` bullets also use a four-line `apply le_of_not_gt; intro h; exact (not_le_of_gt ht) (…mpr h.le)` detour. This is a plain contrapositive of an iff: from `t < τ` one gets `¬ τ ≤ t`, hence `¬ V/2 ≤ v`, hence `v < V/2`. The repetition makes the proof look longer than the idea behind it.
findings.proposed_change:
Rewrite `hh` once after `dsimp only at hh ⊢`, using `rw [← he] at hh`, so that it speaks about `S.Q t ω i`. Then the bullets reduce to:
  · exact hh.1.mp
  · exact fun ht => (not_le.mp (hh.2.1.not.mp ht.not_ge)).le
  · exact hh.2.1.mp
  · exact fun ht => (not_le.mp (hh.2.2.1.not.mp ht.not_ge)).le
The `.not` and `not_le` steps state the contrapositive reasoning directly. If `not_le.mp` is thought too terse, `fun ht => le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge fun h => ht.not_ge (hh.2.1.mpr h))` is an equally short variant. This is untested.
findings.benefit: The single rewrite makes it clear that the same coordinate identity is used throughout, and each bullet becomes one line. A reader sees directly that the two `≤` facts come from the contrapositive of the `τ ≤ t ↔ threshold ≤ v` iff, and that the other two are the forward direction. This removes about 12 lines of repeated `rw [he]` and `intro h` boilerplate without hiding the argument.

findings.problem: The proof builds the existential witness for `List.mem_map` by hand, with `k` and `rfl`, even though the core lemma `List.mem_map_of_mem` proves exactly `f a ∈ map f l` from `a ∈ l`. The `by exact` wrapper is also redundant for a term-mode proof.
findings.proposed_change:
Use the term proof:
  List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (List.mem_map_of_mem (Finset.mem_toList.mpr (Finset.mem_univ k)))
This is untested. The lemma statement is `theorem mem_map_of_mem {f : α → β} (h : a ∈ l) : f a ∈ map f l`.
findings.benefit: The proof now follows the structure of `factorSwitchList` directly: `ρ k` is in the mapped list because `k` is in `univ.toList`, and the list is `0 :: map ρ …`. It no longer needs an anonymous-constructor existential with `rfl`.

evidence.excerpt: theorem mem_map_of_mem {f : α → β} (h : a ∈ l) : f a ∈ map f l := mem_map.2 ⟨_, h, rfl⟩

findings.problem: The membership of the head of a cons list is proved by unfolding the definition and running a simp set. The statement is exactly `List.mem_cons_self` after unfolding `factorSwitchList`, so the simp call is more indirect than needed.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the proof with `List.mem_cons_self`, wrapped in `by unfold factorSwitchList; exact List.mem_cons_self` if the elaborator does not unfold the definition itself. This is untested.
findings.benefit: It names the one fact being used, that the head belongs to its own list, instead of a simp-lemma list. It also parallels the term-mode style of the neighbouring `factorSwitchList_mem`. This is a minor improvement.

evidence.excerpt: theorem mem_cons_self {a : α} {l : List α} : a ∈ a :: l := .head ..
